source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Clearly identify the electrical appliance that failed the safety check:
   - Provide model and serial number
   - Specify the date and time of the test
   - Document the location of the appliance
3. Record the standards or regulations against which the safety check was performed.
   - Include specific reference to the relevant regulations or safety standards (e.g., NFPA 70, IEC 60335, UL, or other local code requirements)
4. Detail the specific checks that were performed:
   - Note each safety check (e.g., visual inspection for damage, continuity test, insulation resistance test, earth continuity test, functional test, etc.)
   - Use a checklist to ensure consistency in your documentation
5. Clearly document the malfunction or failure:
   - Record any alarms, error codes, or issues observed during functionality tests
   - Describe any physical damage or anomalies (e.g., frayed wires, loose screws, overheating) in a detailed
